name: Paystack

status.webhook_verification: Header 'x-paystack-signature'; HMAC-SHA512 of the RAW request body using the merchant SECRET KEY (sk_); no separate webhook secret; RAW bytes required; ack 200 fast (Paystack retries up to 72h)

credentials_required.label: Secret Key (sk_)
credentials_required.note: server-side auth for all API calls AND the HMAC key used to verify webhooks

credentials_required.label: Public Key (pk_)
credentials_required.note: optional — only for Paystack Inline / Popup on the client; not needed for server-side redirect flow

test_credentials.note: Instant test keys on signup from dashboard → Settings → API Keys & Webhooks, no KYC. KYC only required to activate live mode.

sandbox.notes: Test mode only accepts Paystack test cards — real cards are declined in test mode. Test bank: Zenith account 0000000000, OTP 123456. Base URL is the same host (api.paystack.co) for test and live; the sk_test_/sk_live_ key prefix selects the mode.

pain_points.cause: amount must be sent in SUBUNITS (kobo/pesewas/cents) but merchants send major units — NGN 100 sent as 100 instead of 10000
pain_points.mitigation: Expose major units in the ManishaPay API and multiply by 100 to an integer internally; validate the result is a positive integer; never trust the caller to pre-format

pain_points.problem: Marking an unpaid transaction as paid
pain_points.cause: the top-level 'status:true' in a verify response only means the API call succeeded — the real payment outcome is data.status
pain_points.mitigation: Key the normalizer ONLY on data.status (must equal 'success'); additionally re-check data.amount and data.currency against the order before fulfilling

pain_points.cause: HMAC is computed over a re-serialised JSON body instead of the raw bytes, or the wrong key is used
pain_points.mitigation: Compute HMAC-SHA512 over the RAW request buffer (before any JSON parser) using the merchant SECRET KEY, and compare against the x-paystack-signature header with a constant-time compare

pain_points.problem: Missed webhooks on localhost / slow endpoint / CSRF-protected route
pain_points.cause: Paystack cannot reach a local dev URL, times out on a slow handler, or the framework's CSRF filter blocks the POST
pain_points.mitigation: Acknowledge with 200 synchronously and do the work asynchronously; exempt the webhook route from CSRF; make side-effects idempotent on the reference; use verify-poll as a backstop

pain_points.problem: Redirect return beats the webhook (race) — or vice versa
pain_points.cause: the customer's browser redirect (callback_url) and the async webhook are not ordered
pain_points.mitigation: Treat the webhook as primary and verify-poll as a backstop; dedupe both on the unique reference with a monotonic state machine; never gate fulfillment on the browser redirect alone

pain_points.problem: Currency not enabled on the account
pain_points.cause: initializing in a currency the merchant has not activated (e.g. USD/GHS/ZAR/KES) returns a 4xx
pain_points.mitigation: Validate the requested currency against the merchant's enabled currencies and surface a clear resolution message

pain_points.cause: reusing a reference across attempts collides — Paystack requires it to be unique
pain_points.mitigation: Generate a unique reference per attempt and map it to the ManishaPay transaction id; use it as the idempotency key across initiate/verify/webhook

pain_points.problem: Failed recurring charge is not retried
pain_points.cause: Paystack does not automatically retry a failed subscription/charge_authorization
pain_points.mitigation: Implement your own retry/dunning schedule around charge_authorization; monitor invoice.payment_failed events

notes: Zimbabwe is NOT a supported Paystack merchant country — only NG, GH, ZA, KE and CI can register as merchants. It is a regional (not ZW-local) rail useful for ManishaPay merchants operating in those markets or charging in USD. Recurring is supported via charge_authorization (reuse the authorization_code from a verify response for a no-interaction server-side charge) or plans + subscriptions. Refunds via POST /refund (full, or partial by passing amount in subunits).
